subject: Globex RFP: proposed SLA measurement & service credit workplan
messages:
From: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@globex.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2027-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the initial response to our RFP. Procurement and SRE at Globex reviewed Redwood's proposed uptime and latency definitions and have two follow-ups before we can proceed to commercial redlines:

1) Measurement source — we need a clear single source of truth for availability and latency that will be used to calculate credits. Is it Redwood telemetry (Prometheus/Datadog) or will Globex provide client-side sampling?
2) Exclusions — maintenance windows, force majeure, and customer-caused outages need explicit handling.
3) Latency measurement for streaming responses vs non-streaming (completion) requests — request types have different p99 semantics.

Can you provide a short workplan showing the metrics, measurement queries, sampling assumptions, dispute windows, and credit calculation formula? We are on a tight timeline for our SOC/contract sign-off.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Holt
Lead Procurement Manager
Globex Corporation

[attachment: RFP-excerpt_Globex.pdf (pdf)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@globex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear questions. Attached is a concise workplan (PDF) and a plain-text set of sample telemetry queries. High-level answers before you open the attachments:

- Single source of truth: Redwood will declare server-side telemetry as the primary measurement source for SLA calculations (we run an internal Prometheus + aggregator that feeds our SLA engine). If customers want client-side sampling we can ingest that as supplemental evidence during disputes, but not as the primary input unless mutually agreed and instrumented.

- Measurement semantics:
  * Availability (monthly): (successful requests / total requests) excluding planned maintenance windows and excluded origins. Successful requests = 2xx and idempotent 3xx for non-streaming; streaming success defined as connection established + no server-side termination error.
  * Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured on server-side completion time for non-streaming. For streaming use 95th percentile time-to-first-chunk (TTFC) and tail chunk inter-arrival distributions.

- Sampling & granularity: telemetry retained at 1s resolution; SLA engine computes rolling 5-minute buckets aggregated into hourly and monthly windows. For high-volume customers we sample 100% of interactivity by default; for very high throughput we downsample deterministically (hash by request id) with 1-in-N sampling but scale-adjusted to preserve p99 fidelity. Our queries are included in the TXT.

- Dispute window & evidence: 30 calendar days from posting of the monthly SLA report to raise a dispute; evidence exchange via shared Drive and audit logs.

- Credit calculation (preview): credit = min(monthly_commitment, floor( (1 - measured_availability / SLA_threshold) * monthly_fee * credit_multiplier )). Cap at 50% of monthly bill. Full formula and worked examples in the attachment.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to run through the Prometheus queries and dispute process? If procurement wants to change the single-source default to client-side telemetry, we should record that in the mutual action plan and update instrumentation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_SLA_Measurement_Draft_v3.pdf, sample-telemetry-queries.txt

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed tweak to streaming latency clause

Lauren / Karthik —

Reading Samantha's note and our draft, I suggest tightening the streaming latency definition: the RFP folks will likely press for a single p99 latency metric. We should explicitly separate initiation latency (TTFC) and sustained tail (p99 chunk latency). Proposal:

- TTFC measured p95 must be below X ms for the dedicated model class.
- p99 measured on per-chunk inter-arrival times, reported as a distribution; credits only apply to TTFC breaches and server-termination errors, not to intermittent chunk jitter caused by client network.

Rationale: avoids credit exposure for network-level jitter that Redwood can't control, while meeting the customer's need for a sensible tail metric.

Also, for the credit formula, let's add a minimum incident threshold (e.g., event > 5 minutes and > 0.1% request impact) before any credit calculation triggers. Otherwise tiny blips generate credits.

—Ben

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: proposed tweak to streaming latency clause

Ben / Lauren —

Agree with Ben's approach. A couple of implementation notes for the attachment queries:

- Prometheus query for availability (example):
  sum(rate(rl_requests_total{job="inference",code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(rl_requests_total{job="inference"}[5m]))

- For streaming TTFC we instrument request_start and first_chunk_emitted counters and compute histogram of (first_chunk_time - request_time) buckets. We'll include a ready-to-run Grafana panel and the exact histogram thresholds in the PDF.

- Time sync & clock drift: our SLA engine uses server-side TAI timestamps and includes NTP health as part of audit logs. If drift > 2s in a monthly window the affected buckets are flagged and excluded unless otherwise reconciled.

I'll fold these into v3 and push to Drive; planning to update the credit examples with Ben's minimum-incident threshold.

—Karthik

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@globex.com>, procurement@globex.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications (updated workplan + next steps)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is v3 of the SLA measurement workplan (PDF) and a text file with Prometheus queries and sample Grafana panel configs. Highlights of what changed since my earlier note:

- Split streaming metrics into TTFC (p95) and per-chunk tail (p99 distribution). Credits will be tied to TTFC breaches and server-side termination errors only; transient per-chunk jitter attributable to client network is excluded.
- Added minimum-incident criteria before crediting: incident must impact >0.1% of requests in a 5-minute window and last >5 minutes.
- Added detailed disputes workflow: 30-day dispute window, evidence handoff via shared Drive, and a two-week mediation SLA for audit review once a dispute is opened.
- Provided worked credit calculation examples for monthly, weekly, and single-incident scenarios.

Next steps: please confirm availability for a 30-min walkthrough on Thursday Aug 26 at 10:00 PT or propose an alternate time. If Globex wants client-side telemetry to be primary, we'll need a separate instrumentation and validation project timeline (estimated 4–6 weeks).

If you want, we can pull legal in after the walkthrough to translate the workplan into explicit contract language (SLA exhibit).

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_SLA_Measurement_Draft_v3.pdf (updated), sample-telemetry-queries.txt
